name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
one_liner: A locked-down sandbox for AI agents — it lets an AI assistant use real files, tools, and credentials without being able to touch anything it wasn't explicitly allowed to.
buyer: A platform or security engineer at a company rolling out many internal AI coding agents who needs to prove to leadership that an agent can't leak secrets or reach systems it shouldn't.
business_use_cases: An enterprise IT team routes every internal AI agent through OpenShell so none of them ever sees a real API key or touches an unapproved system.
A company building an AI-agent product embeds OpenShell as its safety layer so it can market 'enterprise-grade sandboxing' to risk-averse buyers.
A regulated company (finance, healthcare) uses it so every agent action is policy-enforced and auditable for a compliance review.

money_ideas.idea: Run a hosted OpenShell gateway with a policy dashboard for companies that don't want to self-host their own control plane.
Sell consulting to write and audit the access policies for a company's specific agent fleet.

steal_this: Stand up a hosted OpenShell gateway with a simple policy dashboard and sell it to small AI-agent startups as 'agent safety-as-a-service' before they build their own.
